title: Perfectness of the standard quotients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $n\geq1$ an integer, with $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. For $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $I=(\ell)$, the quotient $P_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z\cong A/I^n$, regarded as an $A$-module in degree zero, is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], represented by
$$[\mathbf Z_\ell\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\mathbf Z_\ell]$$
in degrees $-1$ and $0$. The augmentation in degree zero is the quotient map, followed by the indicated identification with $P_n$.

For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], the analogous complex
$$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}\mathcal O_E]$$
in degrees $-1$ and $0$, augmented by $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n\mathcal O_E$, is a finite free resolution. Thus $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n\mathcal O_E$ is perfect over $\mathcal O_E$ as well. Powers and quotient maps have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and complexes and quasi-isomorphisms that of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

In both cases the quotient is finite as a set. These are precisely the perfectness and finite-set requirements on the ordinary coefficient modules $P_n=A/I^n$ in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; no identification of completed and constant coefficient sheaf categories is asserted. Perfectness here is the ring-module notion of Stacks Tag 0657 (more-algebra-definition-perfect): a module in degree zero is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective modules.

proof.text: Use the canonical PadicInt.toZModPow map. Its kernel is span {l^n}, equal to (span {l})^n by Ideal.span_singleton_pow. The first isomorphism theorem gives the quotient identification with ZMod(l^n), with exactly the required quotient-map equation. For the finite extension, the generator clause of extension_integers_dvr and the nonzero maximal ideal show the recorded uniformizer is nonzero. Both rings are domains (the second is a subring of the field E).

source.place: Proof, coefficient rings and canonical quotient identification

proof.text: For a nonzero scalar a in either domain, multiplication by a is injective. The quotient maps are surjective, and their zero fibers are span {a}. The characterization of membership in a singleton-generated ideal by divisibility proves exactness of A --a--> A --> M. Apply this with a=l^n or uniformizer^n.

source.place: Tag 00PD, principal ideal membership and injectivity of multiplication in a domain

proof.text: Construct HomologicalComplex.double of multiplication by a in degrees -1 and 0. Its canonical degree identifications give the specified differential and make every term finite free; it is zero elsewhere. Construct the augmentation using mkHomFromDouble and the quotient map in degree zero. At degree -1 the source is exact by injectivity, at degree zero the induced homology map is invertible by exactness and surjectivity of the quotient, and elsewhere both homologies are zero. Thus it is a quasi-isomorphism. Localization gives the required isomorphism with precisely this augmentation. Freeness implies projectivity, so the bounded model gives IsPerfectRingComplex.

source.place: Tag 0115; Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 0657, explicit two-term cohomology and finite-projective model

proof.text: The base quotient is finite by the ring equivalence with ZMod(l^n). For the extension use finite_coefficientExtensionRing from the coefficient-extension interface; its defining ideal is exactly the power of the singleton uniformizer ideal. Combine these facts with the two instances of the generic resolution construction.

blueprint_update.statement:
For $A=\Zl$ and $I=(\ell)$, the quotient $P_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ is
perfect over $\Zl$, represented by

$$
 [\Zl\xrightarrow{\ell^n}\Zl]
$$

in degrees $-1$ and $0$, in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The analogous two-term resolution
holds for $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ over the ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ of
a finite extension $E/\Ql$.

proof.text:
A uniformizer is a non-zero-divisor in a complete discrete valuation ring, so
the displayed two-term complex is a finite free resolution of the quotient,
which is therefore perfect as required by
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].
